title: Why Leaves Change Color: Yellow and Orange

scenes.title: HIDDEN COLORS
scenes.caption: Yellow pigments are present before autumn.
scenes.narration: Even green leaves contain yellow and orange pigments. Chlorophyll usually hides them during the growing season.

scenes.title: MEET THE CAROTENOIDS
scenes.caption: Carotenoids create yellow and orange shades.
scenes.narration: Carotenoids are a family of pigments found in leaves and many other parts of plants. They help capture light and protect leaf tissues.

scenes.title: GOLDEN LEAVES
scenes.caption: Less chlorophyll lets yellow shine through.
scenes.narration: When green chlorophyll fades, carotenoids become easier to see. This is why birches, aspens, and many other trees turn yellow.

scenes.title: ORANGE IN THE CANOPY
scenes.caption: Some leaves show a blend of pigments.
scenes.narration: Yellow and orange tones can mix with remaining green or newly formed red pigments. The result depends on the tree and the season.

scenes.title: PIGMENTS AT WORK
scenes.caption: Carotenoids also help protect plant cells.
scenes.narration: These pigments do more than create beautiful colors. They help manage excess light and protect the photosynthetic machinery.

scenes.title: WHY COLORS VARY
scenes.caption: Each species has its own pigment balance.
scenes.narration: Different trees contain different amounts and types of pigments. That is why autumn color varies from bright yellow to deep orange.
